narrative: Spend rose 11.4% to ₹10,405 (from ₹9,344) on 249 leads, up 29.0% from 193 — cost per lead improved again to ₹41.79 (from ₹48.42), holding in the same ₹41-42 band flagged as this tab's best CPL level over the last several reads. CPM (₹62.19) and CTR (1.08%) are both essentially flat against last week, so the lead-volume gain is coming from scale rather than a click-quality shift.

The Advantage+TG split flagged for several weeks running has gone further still: the original ad set 'VP_Lead_inst-form_Advantage+TG_01-04-2026' has fallen to just ₹217 (from ₹6,967), while its 'Copy' now carries almost the entire ₹7,325 of that budget, up from ₹0 the week before. 'VP_Animated-Static_17July26' remains the tab's anchor ad, spend up ₹2,642 to ₹7,250 with CTR improving to 0.90% — confirmed growing for yet another week, alongside frequency now at 1.21 (from 1.17), the same creeping level called out previously.
Hook rate softened to 24.47% (from 25.76%, -5.0%) even as CTR and lead volume both improved — worth flagging as an early creative-fatigue signal on the anchor ad rather than a broader account issue.
actions: The Advantage+TG split has now run for multiple weeks with spend almost entirely absorbed into the Copy ad set (₹217 vs ₹7,325). Consolidate into one ad set rather than continuing to fragment delivery and reporting.
'VP_Animated-Static_17July26' keeps climbing (now ₹7,250) while frequency rises to 1.21. Get a close variant into testing before frequency caps it.
Hook rate dipped 5.0% while CTR held — test a new opening frame or hook on the anchor ad before this becomes a bigger drag.
CPL at ₹41.79 remains near this tab's best level. Keep budget concentrated on the anchor ad and the Advantage+TG Copy rather than the flat 'New House' and 'Gruhpravesh' ad sets still sitting at ₹0.

narrative: For a second straight read since the App Install split, Seemantonayan's corrected numbers confirm this isn't a one-off: spend rose 32.9% to ₹8,005 (from ₹6,026) while chats fell another 21.2% to 223 (from 283), pushing cost per chat up 68.6% to ₹35.90 and CPM up 51.1% to ₹36.71. Both reads since the split now show the same shape — spend up roughly a third, chats down roughly a fifth — confirming this is a real efficiency deterioration rather than noise from the tab reorganization.

'VP_Garbhsanskar_ 27July26' keeps softening on CTR (0.55% to 0.50%), now a fourth consecutive week of decline, even as its spend eased slightly (₹2,098 to ₹2,014). Account-wide CTR fell again to 0.60% (from 0.77%), a new low for this tab. 'Testing_Broad_17Jun26' remains the largest single spend mover for a second week running (+₹1,004 to ₹4,046), and 'VP_Spirituality+Yoga_15Jun26' has emerged as a second major riser (+₹976 to ₹3,959), its CTR also softening (0.86% to 0.72%).
actions: Efficiency decline is now confirmed for a second straight week (chats -21.2%, cost per chat +68.6%). This needs a real intervention this week — pause or hard-cap the ad sets with declining CTR rather than another week of monitoring.
'VP_Garbhsanskar_ 27July26' has now declined for four straight weeks. Pause or replace it rather than continuing to flag it.
CPM up 51.1% and account CTR at a new low (0.60%) both point to audience fatigue — expand into a new interest or lookalike audience rather than adding spend to the same broad testing ad sets.
'Testing_Broad_17Jun26' and 'VP_Spirituality+Yoga_15Jun26' are now the two largest spend movers with softening CTR on both — check performance closely before either grows further.

narrative: Second read for this tab: cumulative spend has grown to ₹1,202 on 122 chats (from ₹1,042 and 116 chats in yesterday's first read), a cost per chat of ₹9.85 — a touch higher than yesterday's ₹8.98 but still dramatically cheaper than Seemantonayan's ₹35.90. CTR (0.88%) and hook rate (26.46%) are essentially unchanged from yesterday's read, a good early sign of stability rather than a one-day fluke.

Spend remains almost entirely on the video creative 'VP_AppDownload_Video1' (₹1,163 of ₹1,202, CTR 0.87%); the static variant 'VP_AppDownload_Static-1' has grown only slightly to ₹39, still too little to read. Only one ad set is running, so there's still no spend-shift pattern to report.

callout.title: Still a small sample — second read
callout.body: Cumulative spend is now ₹1,202 across roughly a week and a half. Numbers are holding stable versus yesterday's first read, which is encouraging, but this is still too early to call a trend — keep treating it as a baseline for another 1-2 weeks.

actions: Cost per chat (₹9.85) is holding in the same range as yesterday's first read — the early efficiency advantage over Seemantonayan looks real, not a fluke. Consider a modest budget increase to test if it holds at scale.
The static creative still has negligible spend (₹39). Push it into real rotation so there's an actual creative comparison within a couple of weeks.
Continue treating this as a baseline — revisit spend-shift diagnostics once there are 2+ ad sets or 2+ weeks of real history.

narrative: The attribution-lag pattern flagged in recent reads keeps closing: Meta now shows 22 purchases against Shopify's 24 confirmed orders for the same window — a gap of just 2, down from the gap of 5 flagged in yesterday's read. Shopify's numbers keep climbing regardless: orders up 100% to 24, revenue up 100% to ₹42,732, and ROAS at 6.94x, essentially matching yesterday's 7.02x — the second-best ROAS this tab has posted.

CTR continued to improve, up to 2.17% from 1.73% (+25.5%), and hook rate rose to 26.57% (+21.6%) — both still accelerating rather than plateauing. Frequency held essentially flat at 1.38 (from 1.39, -1.2%), still no sign of the saturation flagged as a risk two weeks ago.

'VP_Broad_AD+_31jul26' remains the dominant ad set, spend up further to ₹5,990 (from ₹5,269 in yesterday's read) as 'VP_Broad_AD+_10Jun26' keeps fading, now down to just ₹171. At the ad level, 'VP_Umbartha_VideoAD_14-04-2026 – Copy' remains the anchor creative for a fourth straight week, spend up ₹754 to ₹5,524 with CTR climbing again to 2.15%.

callout.title: Attribution lag narrowing — Shopify still the source of truth
callout.body: Meta's purchase count (22) is now much closer to Shopify's confirmed orders (24) than in recent reads — the lag is resolving faster than usual. Keep reading ROAS off Shopify (6.94x) rather than Meta's 'Cost per Purchase,' though the gap is smaller than it's been in weeks.

actions: ROAS is holding at 6.94x, its second-highest read yet, with CTR and hook rate both still climbing. Push another modest budget increase — still no saturation signs.
'VP_Umbartha_VideoAD_14-04-2026 – Copy' has now anchored spend for four straight weeks. Get 1-2 close variants into testing so a fresh option is ready before frequency (1.38) starts capping it.
The Meta/Shopify purchase gap has narrowed to just 2 — a good sign the lag is stabilizing. Watch the next read to confirm rather than assuming it's fully resolved.
'VP_Broad_AD+_10Jun26' is down to ₹171 and effectively retired. Reallocate whatever's left in that ad set to 'VP_Broad_AD+_31jul26'.

narrative: Spend rose 18.6% to ₹12,684 (from ₹10,694) on 52 Meta purchases, up 48.6% from 35 — cost per purchase improved further to ₹244 (from ₹306), down 20.2%, extending the efficiency gain flagged over the last several reports. Shopify confirms it: orders up 31.8% to 58, revenue up 29.0% to ₹45,212, and ROAS climbing to 3.56x (from 3.28x) — a fourth consecutive week of real ROAS improvement (3.16x → 3.36x → 3.48x → 3.56x).

CTR held essentially flat at 1.33% (matching last week's 1.32%), so the purchase growth is coming from scale and efficiency rather than a click-quality shift. Hook rate is the one metric moving the wrong way, down 7.9% to 13.27% (from 14.41%) — a bigger drop than the 5.3% flagged last time, so this soft spot is getting worse rather than stabilizing. Frequency also ticked up to 1.39 (from 1.31, +6.2%), a new watch item worth tracking alongside hook rate.

'VP_Kundali-Namakaran_27Jul26' remains fully dominant at the ad-set level, spend up ₹4,570 to ₹7,167. Its 'VP_Kundali-Namakaran_07-03-2026 – Copy' ad set and the matching 'VP_Kundali-Namkaran_VideoAD_07-03-2026' ad have now both fully zeroed out, confirming the retirement flagged in recent reads. 'VP_Kundali-Namkaran_VideoAD2_07-04-2026' continues climbing (now ₹6,936, from ₹169) with CTR steady around 1.2%, and 'Numerology_Static_13july26' has emerged as a new riser (+₹834 to ₹2,861, CTR up to 1.61%).
actions: Hook rate has now declined for two straight reads and the drop widened (-5.3% then -7.9%). This is no longer a minor soft spot — run a fresh hook/opening-frame test on the top ads this week rather than continuing to just flag it.
Frequency has started climbing (1.31 → 1.39, +6.2%) after sitting flat for weeks. Watch closely; if it keeps rising, get a fresh creative into rotation before it caps delivery.
'VP_Kundali-Namkaran_VideoAD2_07-04-2026' keeps growing on a stable ~1.2% CTR with ROAS still climbing. Good candidate for a modest budget increase.
ROAS has now improved for four straight reads (3.16x → 3.36x → 3.48x → 3.56x). Keep current budget allocation; no reason to pull back.
